raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

When HiCache output goes wrong after a host hit, the cause is hard to localize. It might be the backup, the host layout, a load into the wrong slot, a race with eviction, or a state the backup missed. Today nothing checks that the rows a load-back writes to the GPU are the rows that were backed up for those host slots.

This PR adds an opt-in debug check, `SGLANG_DEBUG_HICACHE_VERIFY=1`. Rows backed up from the GPU through the L2 transfer engine are hashed, and each later load-back of those host slots is checked against the hash, row by row, at a cost that only applies while the variable is set. Host slots filled without a device-to-host backup (by a storage backend or by PD decode host receive) cannot be checked, so the check turns itself off in those setups.

## Modifications

- `python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/hicache_verify.py` (new): `HiCacheVerifier`.
  - **Backup:** after a device-to-host backup finishes, each backed-up device row is hashed (two 64-bit polynomial hashes over the row's bytes, computed on the device). The hash is stored under the row's host slot.
  - **Load:** after a host-to-device load finishes, the loaded device rows are hashed the same way and compared with the hashes stored for their host slots. Mismatches are logged as errors with the host slots. Counts (`written`, `checked`, `mismatch`, `unverified`) are logged at most every 60 s.
  - **Rows covered:** MHA pools (all layers' K and V), MLA pools (all layers' KV), Mamba pools (conv and temporal state), and pools that wrap a `full_kv_pool`. Rows of other pools are counted as unverified, with a one-time warning naming the pool. So are host slots that have no recorded backup, such as packed draft-model layers, which are loaded but not backed up by a transfer of their own.
  - **Memory:** hashes are kept in per-(host pool, device pool) tensors indexed by host slot (16 B per slot), so their memory is bounded by the host pool size. Rows are hashed one layer at a time, in chunks of 64K words against one fixed 1 MiB coefficient table per device, so the hashing temporaries are one layer's copy of the rows plus 1 MiB per row, whatever the all-layer row size (Mamba temporal state included).
- `python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/l2_transfer.py`: `L2TransferEngine` builds the verifier when the variable is set. `submit_device_to_host` and `submit_host_to_device` wait for the transfer's finish event and pass the submitted transfers to it. The HiCache controllers, the unified radix cache and the Mamba component back up and load through these two methods. With the variable unset, the only change is one `is not None` check per submission.
- `python/sglang/srt/managers/cache_controller.py` and `python/sglang/srt/disaggregation/decode.py`: attaching a storage (L3) backend, or enabling PD decode host receive (`--disaggregation-decode-host-receive-threshold` below 1), turns the check off with one warning. Storage prefetch and the prefill peer write host slots directly, without a device-to-host backup, so a reused slot would still carry the previous occupant's hash and its load-back would be reported as a false mismatch.
- `python/sglang/srt/environ.py`: `SGLANG_DEBUG_HICACHE_VERIFY = EnvBool(False)` in the debugging section.
- `docs/docs/references/environment_variables.mdx`: a row for the new variable.
- `test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_hicache_verify.py` (new, CPU):
  - a backup and load round trip through `L2TransferEngine` is checked;
  - a host row with one flipped bit is reported as a mismatch;
  - Mamba conv/temporal rows are covered;
  - slots without a backup and unsupported pools count as unverified;
  - a flipped byte in the last chunk of a multi-chunk row is reported;
  - turning the check off (as a storage attach does) leaves transfers working;
  - the check is off by default.
- `test_decode_retraction_backup.py`: enabling decode host receive turns the check off. `test_hicache_storage_registration_hook.py`: attaching a storage backend turns it off.
- `test_hicache_storage_registration_hook.py`, `test_hicache_dcp_host_pool.py`, `test_hicache_unified_key_scheme.py`: their controller stubs, built without `__init__`, gain the `l2_transfer_engine` attribute that `attach_storage_backend` now reads.

## Accuracy Tests

The check only reads rows after transfers finish. With the variable unset, the code path is unchanged.

Each model ran a 16-conversation x 6-turn shared-prefix workload with HiCache, then re-sent the first turn after 65 s idle. The re-send makes the device evict prefixes to the host and load them back. Greedy decoding, same server args with the check on and off.

| Model | GPU | HiCache args | Rows checked (last periodic count) | Mismatches | Cached tokens on / off |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct (MHA) | RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell | `--hicache-ratio 4 --max-total-tokens 16384` | 70,570 | 0 | 242,959 / 242,959 |
| Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B (GDN hybrid: KV + Mamba state) | H100 80GB | `--hicache-size 16 --max-total-tokens 16384 --max-mamba-cache-size 96 --mamba-radix-cache-strategy extra_buffer` | 67,075 | 0 | 218,644 / 218,644 |

Generated text with the check on agrees with the check off within the agreement of two check-off runs (Qwen3.5-4B: 74/96 on vs off, 70/96 off vs off; Qwen2.5-0.5B: 73/96 vs 77/96). Neither model is repeat-deterministic with the radix cache on. `--enable-deterministic-inference` turns the radix cache off, which HiCache does not allow.


## Speed Tests and Profiling

No speed claim. The check is off by default and adds one `is not None` test per transfer submission when off. When on, it synchronizes the transfer stream on every backup and load, so it is meant for debugging, not production serving.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). Accuracy: outputs with the check on and off are compared above; no speed claim (debug option, off by default).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

Prepared with the help of Claude Code; every result above was measured as described.

## Review and Merge Process

1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process).
2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers.
3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so.
   - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci`
4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR.

@@ -0,0 +1,219 @@
+"""Debug check that HiCache load-backs restore exactly the bytes that were backed up.
+
+Enabled with SGLANG_DEBUG_HICACHE_VERIFY=1. The L2 transfer engine waits for
+every device-to-host backup and records a 128-bit hash of each backed-up
+device row under its host slot. After every host-to-device load it hashes the
+loaded device rows and compares them with the hashes recorded for their host
+slots. Any changed byte changes the hash.
+
+Rows are read from MHA (K/V), MLA (KV) and Mamba (conv/temporal) device pools.
+Rows of other pools, and host slots with no recorded backup (for example
+packed draft-model layers, which have no backup transfer of their own), are
+counted as unverified. Every check synchronizes the transfer stream, so this
+is for debugging only. Host slots filled from a storage backend, or by a
+prefill peer under PD decode host receive, never pass a device-to-host backup,
+so the check is turned off when either is in use.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import functools
+import logging
+import random
+import time
+from collections import Counter
+from typing import Callable, Iterator, Optional
+
+import torch
+
+from sglang.srt.mem_cache.memory_pool import MambaPool
+
+logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
+
+_STATS_INTERVAL_S = 60.0
+# int64 words of each row hashed per step; bounds the temporaries to
+# num_rows * 2 * _CHUNK_WORDS * 8 bytes, whatever the row size.
+_CHUNK_WORDS = 1 << 16
+
+
+def _row_parts(pool, rows: torch.Tensor) -> Optional[Iterator[torch.Tensor]]:
+    """The device rows' state as [n, ...] tensors, one layer at a time, or
+    None for an unsupported pool."""
+    if isinstance(pool, MambaPool):
+        cache = pool.mamba_cache
+        return (
+            state[layer, rows]
+            for state in (*cache.conv, cache.temporal)
+            for layer in range(state.shape[0])
+        )
+    # MHATokenToKVPool and its subclasses: one K and one V buffer per layer
+    k_buffer = getattr(pool, "k_buffer", None)
+    if k_buffer is not None:
+        v_buffer = getattr(pool, "v_buffer", None)
+        buffers = [*k_buffer, *(v_buffer if v_buffer is not None else ())]
+        return (buf[rows] for buf in buffers)
+    # MLATokenToKVPool and its subclasses: one KV buffer per layer
+    kv_buffer = getattr(pool, "kv_buffer", None)
+    if kv_buffer is not None:
+        return (buf[rows] for buf in kv_buffer)
+    # HybridLinearKVPool and SWAKVPool: rows of the wrapped full-attention pool
+    full_kv_pool = getattr(pool, "full_kv_pool", None)
+    if full_kv_pool is not None:
+        return _row_parts(full_kv_pool, rows)
+    return None
+
+
+@functools.lru_cache(maxsize=8)
+def _coeffs(device: torch.device) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """[2, _CHUNK_WORDS] fixed odd int64 multipliers, one row per hash lane."""
+    gen = torch.Generator(device="cpu").manual_seed(0)
+    coeffs = torch.randint(
+        -(1 << 62), 1 << 62, (2, _CHUNK_WORDS), generator=gen, dtype=torch.int64
+    )
+    return (coeffs | 1).to(device)
+
+
+@functools.lru_cache(maxsize=4096)
+def _chunk_multipliers(part: int, chunk: int) -> tuple[int, int]:
+    """Two odd multipliers that tie a chunk's sums to its part and position."""
+    rng = random.Random(part * 1_000_003 + chunk)
+    return rng.getrandbits(62) | 1, rng.getrandbits(62) | 1
+
+
+def _row_hashes(
+    parts: Iterator[torch.Tensor], num_rows: int, device: torch.device
+) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """[n, 2] int64: two polynomial hashes (wrapping) over each row's bytes."""
+    hashes = torch.zeros(num_rows, 2, dtype=torch.int64, device=device)
+    coeffs = _coeffs(device)
+    for index, part in enumerate(parts):
+        row_bytes = part.contiguous().view(torch.uint8).reshape(num_rows, -1)
+        pad = (-row_bytes.shape[1]) % 8
+        if pad:
+            row_bytes = torch.nn.functional.pad(row_bytes, (0, pad))
+        words = row_bytes.view(torch.int64)
+        for chunk, start in enumerate(range(0, words.shape[1], _CHUNK_WORDS)):
+            block = words[:, start : start + _CHUNK_WORDS]
+            sums = (block.unsqueeze(1) * coeffs[:, : block.shape[1]]).sum(dim=2)
+            for lane, multiplier in enumerate(_chunk_multipliers(index, chunk)):
+                hashes[:, lane] += sums[:, lane] * multiplier
+    return hashes.cpu()
+
+
+class _HashTable:
+    """Hashes of backed-up rows, indexed by host slot; grows on demand."""
+
+    def __init__(self):
+        self.hashes = torch.zeros(0, 2, dtype=torch.int64)
+        self.valid = torch.zeros(0, dtype=torch.bool)
+
+    def put(self, slots: torch.Tensor, hashes: torch.Tensor) -> None:
+        size = int(slots.max()) + 1
+        if size > self.valid.numel():
+            size = max(size, 2 * self.valid.numel())
+            grown = torch.zeros(size, 2, dtype=torch.int64)
+            grown[: self.hashes.shape[0]] = self.hashes
+            valid = torch.zeros(size, dtype=torch.bool)
+            valid[: self.valid.numel()] = self.valid
+            self.hashes, self.valid = grown, valid
+        self.hashes[slots] = hashes
+        self.valid[slots] = True
+
+    def get(self, slots: torch.Tensor) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
+        """(known, hashes): which slots have a record, and their hashes."""
+        known = torch.zeros(slots.numel(), dtype=torch.bool)
+        hashes = torch.zeros(slots.numel(), 2, dtype=torch.int64)
+        in_range = slots < self.valid.numel()
+        known[in_range] = self.valid[slots[in_range]]
+        hashes[known] = self.hashes[slots[known]]
+        return known, hashes
+
+
+class HiCacheVerifier:
+    """Records backed-up rows and checks loaded ones.
+
+    Callers pass the transfers after they finished. `resolve_rows` maps a
+    transfer to the device rows its pool indexes.
+    """
+
+    def __init__(self, resolve_rows: Callable[..., torch.Tensor]):
+        self._resolve_rows = resolve_rows
+        self._tables: dict[tuple[int, int], _HashTable] = {}
+        self._unsupported: set[str] = set()
+        self._last_stats = time.monotonic()
+        self.counts: Counter[str] = Counter()
+
+    def _hashes(self, transfer) -> Optional[tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]]:
+        """(host slots, row hashes), or None for an unsupported pool."""
+        pool = transfer.device_pool
+        rows = self._resolve_rows(transfer)
+        rows = rows.to(device=_pool_device(pool), dtype=torch.int64)
+        parts = _row_parts(pool, rows)
+        if parts is None:
+            name = type(pool).__name__
+            if name not in self._unsupported:
+                self._unsupported.add(name)
+                logger.warning("HiCache verify: rows of %s are not checked", name)
+            return None
+        slots = transfer.host_indices.to(device="cpu", dtype=torch.int64)
+        return slots, _row_hashes(parts, num_rows=rows.shape[0], device=rows.device)
+
+    def _table(self, transfer) -> _HashTable:
+        key = (id(transfer.host_pool), id(transfer.device_pool))
+        if key not in self._tables:
+            self._tables[key] = _HashTable()
+        return self._tables[key]
+
+    def record_backup(self, transfers) -> None:
+        for transfer in transfers:
+            if transfer.host_indices.numel() == 0:
+                continue
+            result = self._hashes(transfer)
+            if result is None:
+                self.counts["unsupported_written"] += transfer.host_indices.numel()
+                continue
+            slots, hashes = result
+            self._table(transfer).put(slots, hashes)
+            self.counts["written"] += slots.numel()
+        self._maybe_log_stats()
+
+    def check_load(self, transfers) -> None:
+        for transfer in transfers:
+            if transfer.host_indices.numel() == 0:
+                continue
+            result = self._hashes(transfer)
+            if result is None:
+                self.counts["unverified"] += transfer.host_indices.numel()
+                continue
+            slots, hashes = result
+            known, expected = self._table(transfer).get(slots)
+            bad = known & (hashes != expected).any(dim=1)
+            num_bad = int(bad.sum())
+            self.counts["checked"] += int(known.sum())
+            self.counts["unverified"] += int((~known).sum())
+            self.counts["mismatch"] += num_bad
+            if num_bad:
+                logger.error(
+                    "HiCache verify: %d of %d rows loaded into %s differ from their "
+                    "backup (host slots %s)",
+                    num_bad,
+                    slots.numel(),
+                    type(transfer.device_pool).__name__,
+                    slots[bad][:8].tolist(),
+                )
+        self._maybe_log_stats()
+
+    def _maybe_log_stats(self) -> None:
+        now = time.monotonic()
+        if now - self._last_stats >= _STATS_INTERVAL_S:
+            self._last_stats = now
+            logger.info(
+                "HiCache verify: %s",
+                " ".join(f"{k}={v}" for k, v in sorted(self.counts.items())),
+            )
+
+
+def _pool_device(pool) -> torch.device:
+    if isinstance(pool, MambaPool):
+        return pool.mamba_cache.temporal.device
+    return torch.device(getattr(pool, "device", "cpu"))

+"""CPU tests for the SGLANG_DEBUG_HICACHE_VERIFY load-back check.
+
+Turns red if the transfer engine stops recording backups or checking loads,
+or if the row hash stops covering every byte of a K/V or Mamba row.
+"""
+
+import unittest
+from contextlib import contextmanager
+from types import SimpleNamespace
+from unittest import mock
+
+import torch
+
+from sglang.srt.environ import envs
+from sglang.srt.mem_cache import hicache_verify as verify_module
+from sglang.srt.mem_cache import l2_transfer as transfer_module
+from sglang.srt.mem_cache.hicache_verify import HiCacheVerifier
+from sglang.srt.mem_cache.l2_transfer import L2Transfer, L2TransferEngine
+from sglang.srt.mem_cache.memory_pool import MambaPool
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cpu_ci
+from sglang.test.test_utils import CustomTestCase
+
+register_cpu_ci(est_time=8, suite="base-a-test-cpu")
+
+
+class _FakeEvent:
+    def __init__(self, enable_timing=False):
+        self.enable_timing = enable_timing
+
+    def record(self):
+        pass
+
+    def wait(self, stream):
+        pass
+
+    def synchronize(self):
+        pass
+
+
+class _FakeDeviceModule:
+    Event = _FakeEvent
+
+    @staticmethod
+    def Stream():
+        return object()
+
+    @staticmethod
+    @contextmanager
+    def stream(stream):
+        yield
+
+
+class _CopyHostPool:
+    """Keeps backed-up K/V rows by host slot; `corrupt` flips a byte of one slot."""
+
+    layer_num = 1
+
+    def __init__(self):
+        self.rows = {}
+
+    def prepare_transfer_indices(self, host_indices, device_indices, io_backend):
+        return host_indices, device_indices
+
+    def backup_from_device_all_layer_physical(
+        self, device_pool, host_indices, device_indices, io_backend
+    ):
+        for host, device in zip(host_indices.tolist(), device_indices.tolist()):
+            self.rows[host] = (
+                device_pool.k_buffer[0][device].clone(),
+                device_pool.v_buffer[0][device].clone(),
+            )
+
+    def load_to_device_per_layer_physical(
+        self,
+        device_pool,
+        host_indices,
+        device_indices,
+        layer_id,
+        io_backend,
+        is_draft=False,
+    ):
+        for host, device in zip(host_indices.tolist(), device_indices.tolist()):
+            device_pool.k_buffer[0][device] = self.rows[host][0]
+            device_pool.v_buffer[0][device] = self.rows[host][1]
+
+    def corrupt(self, host):
+        self.rows[host][1].view(torch.uint8).view(-1)[3] ^= 1
+
+
+def _mha_pool(num_rows=8):
+    return SimpleNamespace(
+        k_buffer=[torch.randn(num_rows, 2, 4, dtype=torch.bfloat16)],
+        v_buffer=[torch.randn(num_rows, 2, 4, dtype=torch.bfloat16)],
+        device="cpu",
+    )
+
+
+def _mamba_pool(num_slots=6):
+    pool = object.__new__(MambaPool)
+    pool.mamba_cache = SimpleNamespace(
+        conv=[torch.randn(2, num_slots, 3, 2)],
+        temporal=torch.randn(2, num_slots, 2, 4, 4),
+    )
+    return pool
+
+
+def _device_indices(transfer):
+    return transfer.device_indices
+
+
+def _transfer(host_pool, device_pool, host, device):
+    return L2Transfer(
+        host_pool=host_pool,
+        device_pool=device_pool,
+        host_indices=torch.tensor(host),
+        device_indices=torch.tensor(device),
+    )
+
+
+class TestHiCacheVerify(CustomTestCase):
+    def setUp(self):
+        transfer_module._timing_events_supported.cache_clear()
+        self.addCleanup(transfer_module._timing_events_supported.cache_clear)
+        patcher = mock.patch.object(transfer_module, "device_module", _FakeDeviceModule)
+        patcher.start()
+        self.addCleanup(patcher.stop)
+
+    def _engine(self):
+        with envs.SGLANG_DEBUG_HICACHE_VERIFY.override(True):
+            return L2TransferEngine("kernel")
+
+    def test_disabled_by_default(self):
+        self.assertIsNone(L2TransferEngine("kernel")._verifier)
+
+    def test_engine_checks_every_load_back(self):
+        engine, host_pool, device_pool = self._engine(), _CopyHostPool(), _mha_pool()
+        engine.submit_device_to_host(
+            [_transfer(host_pool, device_pool, [10, 11, 12], [0, 1, 2])]
+        )
+        engine.submit_host_to_device(
+            [_transfer(host_pool, device_pool, [10, 11, 12], [5, 6, 7])],
+            transfer_layer_id_max=1,
+        )
+        counts = engine._verifier.counts
+        self.assertEqual((counts["checked"], counts["mismatch"]), (3, 0))
+
+        host_pool.corrupt(11)
+        with self.assertLogs("sglang.srt.mem_cache.hicache_verify", "ERROR"):
+            engine.submit_host_to_device(
+                [_transfer(host_pool, device_pool, [10, 11], [3, 4])],
+                transfer_layer_id_max=1,
+            )
+        self.assertEqual((counts["checked"], counts["mismatch"]), (5, 1))
+
+    def test_mamba_rows_and_slots_without_backup(self):
+        verifier = HiCacheVerifier(resolve_rows=_device_indices)
+        host_pool, pool = object(), _mamba_pool()
+        verifier.record_backup([_transfer(host_pool, pool, [0, 1], [0, 1])])
+        cache = pool.mamba_cache
+        for state in (*cache.conv, cache.temporal):
+            state[:, [2, 3]] = state[:, [0, 1]]
+        cache.temporal[1, 3, 0, 0, 0] += 1
+
+        verifier.check_load([_transfer(host_pool, pool, [0, 1, 7], [2, 3, 4])])
+
+        counts = verifier.counts
+        self.assertEqual(
+            (counts["checked"], counts["mismatch"], counts["unverified"]), (2, 1, 1)
+        )
+
+    def test_every_chunk_of_a_row_is_hashed(self):
+        verify_module._coeffs.cache_clear()
+        self.addCleanup(verify_module._coeffs.cache_clear)
+        verifier = HiCacheVerifier(resolve_rows=_device_indices)
+        host_pool = object()
+        pool = SimpleNamespace(
+            k_buffer=[torch.randn(4, 4, 8, dtype=torch.bfloat16)],
+            v_buffer=[torch.randn(4, 4, 8, dtype=torch.bfloat16)],
+            device="cpu",
+        )
+        with mock.patch.object(verify_module, "_CHUNK_WORDS", 2):
+            verifier.record_backup([_transfer(host_pool, pool, [0, 1], [0, 1])])
+            for buf in (*pool.k_buffer, *pool.v_buffer):
+                buf[[2, 3]] = buf[[0, 1]]
+            pool.k_buffer[0][3].view(torch.uint8).view(-1)[60] ^= 1
+            verifier.check_load([_transfer(host_pool, pool, [0, 1], [2, 3])])
+        counts = verifier.counts
+        self.assertEqual((counts["checked"], counts["mismatch"]), (2, 1))
+
+    def test_storage_backend_turns_the_check_off(self):
+        engine, host_pool, device_pool = self._engine(), _CopyHostPool(), _mha_pool()
+        with self.assertLogs("sglang.srt.mem_cache.l2_transfer", "WARNING"):
+            engine.disable_verifier(reason="a storage backend is attached")
+        self.assertIsNone(engine._verifier)
+        engine.submit_device_to_host(
+            [_transfer(host_pool, device_pool, [10, 11], [0, 1])]
+        )
+        engine.submit_host_to_device(
+            [_transfer(host_pool, device_pool, [10, 11], [5, 6])],
+            transfer_layer_id_max=1,
+        )
+
+    def test_unsupported_pool_rows_are_unverified(self):
+        verifier = HiCacheVerifier(resolve_rows=_device_indices)
+        pool = SimpleNamespace(device="cpu")
+        verifier.record_backup([_transfer(object(), pool, [0, 1], [0, 1])])
+        verifier.check_load([_transfer(object(), pool, [0, 1], [2, 3])])
+        self.assertEqual(verifier.counts["checked"], 0)
+        self.assertEqual(verifier.counts["unverified"], 2)
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    unittest.main()
